headline: BOTH ITEMS ARE DONE AND I CONFIRMED THEM BY MEASUREMENT, AND THE FOUR-RULE GUARD IS ALSO DEFEATED BY FOUR ROUTES IT DOES NOT COVER, TWO OF WHICH I CARRIED THROUGH A GREEN GATE. WHAT IS RIGHT: the shipped stage at cfae9b2 reads no environment, which I established by reading all 178 lines and by running the guard on the text (findings list EMPTY). All FOUR teeth die on the rule claimed and on no other, each producing exactly ONE finding, targets unique: the shell-half `${WARP_LINT_SKIP:-}` branch on the SHELL PIN, `sh -c` on the ARGV SHAPE, `bash -c` on the ARGV SHAPE, `import os` on the CLOSED IMPORT SET. The on-disk figure reproduces EXACTLY: the two round-3 survivors written into scripts/check_lint.sh at cfae9b2 give 3199 passed / 1 failed and exit 1, the dying assertion is the both-halves guard, against a 3200 / 0 baseline in the same worktree, and the stage restores byte-identical (sha256 4732323acec47152 in all three worktrees and in the main tree). The shell pin covers the WHOLE half, not four named lines: the half is 68 lines of which 4 are non-comment, a fifth line after the `PY` terminator is caught, an unquoted heredoc delimiter is caught, and a renamed delimiter or a changed `exec` line fails CLOSED through the parse rule. CDPATH reproduces at 405d3b3 (`lint: pass (1 python, 1 shell, 0.00s)` exit 0 over the eight-defect fixture tree, having linted the decoy; `lint: pass (1 python, 0 shell, 0.00s)` exit 0 over the real repository) and is CLOSED at cfae9b2 (`lint: FAIL (8 python, 2 shell)` exit 1 with the same variable set). WHAT IS NOT: the guard's own docstring at scripts/selftest.py:20759 claims `Every route by which this stage's TEXT could come to read the environment', and FOUR routes produce an EMPTY findings list while reading the environment and reporting a pass over a tree carrying eight planted defects. The sharpest is not obfuscation, it is an ordinary refactor: `_r = subprocess.run` followed by `_r(["sh", "-c", 'test -n "$WARP_OFF"'])`, because the argv rule at :20791 only inspects calls whose func is an Attribute on the Name `subprocess`. MEASURED ON DISK AT cfae9b2: selftest 3200 passed / 0 failed and `./scripts/verify.sh` GATE: GREEN exit 0, with the stage carrying a live fail-open switch. The other three are a split-literal `open("/proc/self/envi" "ron")` (3200 / 0 on disk), `vars(subprocess)["o" "s"]` and `sys.modules["o" "s"]` with a split attribute name. SEPARATELY, A FOURTH ENVIRONMENT CLASS DEFEATS THE SHIPPED TEXT AND IS DECLARED NOWHERE: `GIT_DIR=<an empty repository>/.git bash scripts/check_lint.sh` prints `lint: pass (0 python, 0 shell, 0.00s)` and exits 0 over the same eight-defect tree, and GIT_INDEX_FILE does the same, because the whitelisted `("git", "ls-files")` shape at scripts/check_lint.sh:91 IS a subprocess that reads the environment. That falsifies `so it can neither read the environment directly nor shell out to something that will' at scripts/check_lint.sh:51 to :53, and `Three classes do' in the manifest's assertion_integrity. NEITHER IS BLOCKING and I checked each leg: the shipped stage reads no environment, so the narrowed sentence `no environment variable THE STAGE READS can make it report success' is TRUE as written; GIT_DIR defeats the per-file loop at 0de75f3e IDENTICALLY (`lint: pass` exit 0, measured), so nothing regressed and no surface was added; round 2 settled the whole class of an attacker who can write the gate's environment as non-blocking; and round 3 ruled the identical shape (a measurable, closeable, undeclared fail-open in the stage's own text) a NOTE owing a sentence rather than a round. NO BLOCKING DEFECT. What is owed is two sentence edits and, if the owner wants it closed rather than declared, `env=` on two subprocess calls. THE FLOOR IS CLEAN ON EVERY ITEM, on my own gate run: GATE: GREEN at 2fd3d21, 3200 passed / 0 failed, 3:08.66.

The guard run on that text returns an EMPTY findings list. No tooth dies incidentally on another rule and none dies on two. Targets: each occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the stage (I re-counted), and T2 and T3 share one insertion point by design, which is what the assertion claims. Expectations are enumerated constants (`_L07_SHELL_PINNED`, `_L07_PY_IMPORTS`, `_L07_ARGV_SHAPES`, `_L07_ENV_TOKENS`) and not derived from the code under test, and the guard is non-vacuous in both directions: EMPTY for the shipped text, NON-EMPTY for the round-2 ambient revision. (3) THE ON-DISK FIGURE REPRODUCES EXACTLY: in detached worktrees at cfae9b2 the unmutated `python3 scripts/selftest.py` is 3200 passed / 0 failed exit 0; with the shell-half branch written into scripts/check_lint.sh it is 3199 passed / 1 failed exit 1; with the `sh -c` read it is 3199 passed / 1 failed exit 1; the dying assertion in both is the both-halves guard, and after `git checkout --` the stage is byte-identical (sha256 4732323acec4715221d9700a8a60996b9dd17e71b6491bfe6f44752da8b7a762) in all three worktrees and in the main tree. (4) THE SHELL PIN COVERS THE WHOLE HALF: `_l07_halves` partitions all 178 lines into 68 shell and 110 python with none lost, comments and blanks are excluded so the 60-line header is editable, a fifth non-comment line placed AFTER the `PY` terminator is caught by the pin, a shell branch placed BETWEEN two `PY` lines lands in the python half and is caught by the parse rule, an unquoted `<<PY` delimiter is caught, and renaming the delimiter or the `exec` line makes the whole text the shell half, which also fails. Every miss I could construct fails CLOSED. (5) WHAT IS NOT CLOSED is N1 and N2 and is not an AC2 failure: four routes give an EMPTY findings list while reading the environment and reporting a pass, and a fourth environment class (GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE) defeats the shipped text through the whitelisted `git ls-files` shape. The property AC2 binds to holds AT THIS REVISION, which I verified by reading the text rather than by trusting the list, and the class that defeats it defeats the per-file loop identically.

spec_edit_ruling: NO SPEC EDIT WAS MADE THIS ROUND AND I VERIFIED IT MECHANICALLY. `git log --oneline 405d3b3..2fd3d21 -- specs/WARP-0711-lint-one-interpreter.md specs/index.md` is EMPTY, so neither the spec nor the index moved after the round-3 review, and the three spec defects the earlier rounds recorded are untouched and remain the owner's: the AC3 clause with its two dead footprint globs (plugin/templates/scripts/check_lint.sh and packs/*/scripts/check_lint.sh, neither of which exists), `placement: [engine]` which no footprint path resolves to, and the risk sentence's 'gate stage plus its seven engine copies'. The item's own assertion at scripts/selftest.py binds the PLACEMENT RELATIONSHIP rather than pinning the wrong value, so a legitimate correction of the placement will not turn the gate red, which is the right shape and I am not reopening it.
notes: N1 FOUR ROUTES DEFEAT THE FOUR-RULE GUARD, AND I CARRIED TWO OF THEM THROUGH A GREEN GATE. The docstring at scripts/selftest.py:20759 reads `Every route by which this stage's TEXT could come to read the environment, as a list of findings over BOTH halves. EMPTY means no route is present.' That is a universal and it is false. MEASURED, each mutant written into scripts/check_lint.sh in a detached worktree at cfae9b2, the guard's findings list printed, then the suite run to completion, then the mutated stage run over a fixture repository carrying eight planted defects with its trigger variable exported: (a) `_r = subprocess.run` followed by `_r(["sh", "-c", 'test -n "$WARP_OFF"'])` gives an EMPTY findings list, `python3 scripts/selftest.py` 3200 passed / 0 failed, `./scripts/verify.sh` GATE: GREEN exit 0 with `lint: pass (694 python, 172 shell, 0.83s)`, and `WARP_OFF=1` over the eight-defect tree `lint: pass` exit 0. The argv rule at :20791 only inspects Calls whose func is an Attribute on the Name `subprocess`, so ANY alias of subprocess.run is outside it, and an alias is an ordinary refactor rather than an obfuscation. (b) `open("/proc/self/envi" "ron", "rb")` gives an EMPTY findings list and 3200 passed / 0 failed on disk with the same fail-open; the LITERAL spelling `open("/proc/self/environ")` IS caught, on the token rule, because `environ' is a substring, so the guard catches the spelling a reviewer would try and misses the one an adversary would write. (c) `vars(subprocess)["o" "s"]` plus `getattr(_m, "envi" "ron")` and (d) `sys.modules["o" "s"]` plus the same split attribute both give EMPTY findings lists and both fail open: `os` is reachable through two modules that are INSIDE the closed declared set, so rule 3 does not bound what the python half can reach, only what it can name in an import statement. WHY THIS IS A NOTE AND NOT A BLOCK: the property AC2 binds to is a property of the SHIPPED text, and the shipped text reads no environment, which I verified by reading it rather than by trusting the guard. Round 3 found the identical situation (two spellings evading its text guard) and ruled it `a future-regression gap and not a present defect', which I am applying consistently. WHAT IS OWED IS A SENTENCE, NOT A ROUND: the manifest's own AC2 evidence[1] already states the honest form, `FOUR ROUTES, each closed by one rule', and the docstring should say the same instead of `Every route'. If the owner wants the gap narrowed as well as the sentence corrected, the two cheapest conjuncts are (i) treat any Name bound to a `subprocess` attribute as a subprocess call, or simply forbid assigning a subprocess attribute to a name, and (ii) run the token scan over the CONCATENATED string constants of the AST rather than over raw source lines, which kills every split-literal spelling at once. Neither is a redesign.

N2 A FOURTH ENVIRONMENT CLASS DEFEATS THE SHIPPED STAGE, IT IS DECLARED NOWHERE, AND IT IS THE ONE CLASS THAT IS CLOSEABLE. MEASURED at cfae9b2 over a fixture repository carrying eight planted defects, no mutation of any kind: `GIT_DIR=<an empty git repository>/.git bash scripts/check_lint.sh` prints `lint: pass (0 python, 0 shell, 0.00s)` and exits 0, and `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<that repository's index>` does the same. GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES do not (both `lint: FAIL (8 python, 2 shell)` exit 1, so this is the two variables and not the family). The mechanism is the stage's own text: `subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", pattern], check=True, ...)` at scripts/check_lint.sh:91 is a subprocess that READS THE ENVIRONMENT, and it is one of the two shapes rule 4 WHITELISTS. That falsifies three sentences. (1) scripts/check_lint.sh:51 to :53, `its two subprocess argument vectors are pinned by shape, so it can neither read the environment directly nor shell out to something that will' - it does shell out to something that will, by design, twice. (2) The manifest's assertion_integrity, `THE ONE CLAIM THIS ROUND DELIBERATELY DOES NOT MAKE: that no environment variable of any kind can defeat this stage. Three classes do, one is closed and two are declared' - FOUR do. (3) assumptions[1], `CDPATH was the third and the only one that ran through this stage's own text' - GIT_DIR runs through :91. WHY THIS IS A NOTE AND NOT A BLOCK, and I checked each leg: the narrowed sentence the round exists to install, `no environment variable THE STAGE READS can make it report success, and it reads none', is TRUE as written, because the stage does not read GIT_DIR, git does; the per-file loop at 0de75f3e ALSO ran `git ls-files`, and I measured GIT_DIR turning it into `lint: pass` exit 0 identically, so nothing regressed and no surface was added; round 2 settled the class of an attacker who can write the gate's environment as non-blocking (`can subvert the gate more directly through PATH'); and round 3 ruled the identical shape a note. THERE IS A REAL ASYMMETRY WITH THE DECLARED LIMITS, though, and it is why this is worth writing down: BASH_ENV and PYTHONPATH are declared because they CANNOT be closed from inside the script, and I verified both (BASH_ENV `lint: pass' exit 0, PYTHONPATH shadowing `subprocess' `lint: pass' exit 0). GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE CAN be closed from inside, in one keyword: pass `env=` to the two subprocess calls with the GIT_* names stripped, or run `git --git-dir=. --work-tree=. ls-files`. So the honest options are to close it the way CDPATH was closed, or to name it in the header beside BASH_ENV. What it must not be is claimed away by a `Three classes' count, which is the same failure mode round 3 recorded against `no environment variable can make this stage report success'. ONE MITIGATION THE ROUND EARNED: the stage's per-language COUNTS make this visible in the gate log as `(0 python, 0 shell)`, where the per-file loop printed a bare `lint: pass', so the observability this item added is what would catch it in practice.

N3 THE LINE-FOR-LINE SHELL PIN IS NOT A MAINTENANCE TRAP, AND I RULE IT ACCEPTABLE; THE DIAGNOSTIC IS THE PART THAT WILL GET THE ASSERTION DELETED. WHY IT IS NOT THE CORPUS-COUNT CLASS, measured rather than argued: the pin reads only scripts/check_lint.sh's own shell half, so NO unrelated work can turn it red, which is the exact property the corpus-count pin lacked (that one was keyed to `git ls-files` output and any added file moved it). The half is 68 lines of which FOUR are non-comment; comment and blank lines are filtered, so the 60-line header can be rewritten freely and I verified that inserting a comment line changes nothing. A legitimate edit to those four lines is close to unimaginable (`set -u`, the `cd`, the heredoc opener, the terminator) and is exactly the edit that should force a human to look, so pinning is the point and it is correctly placed. THE PROBLEM IS THE MESSAGE. `_l07_env_findings` computes a precise diagnostic and the assertion THROWS IT AWAY: `expect(name, condition)` prints only the label, so a future editor sees one 90-word sentence and must go read the function to learn WHICH of the four rules fired and what the actual difference was. Worse, that ONE label covers all four rules plus the two ambient-marker conjuncts, so six different causes produce a byte-identical failure message, and the most likely legitimate trip is not the shell half at all but the CLOSED IMPORT SET, where adding any module for any reason fails with a message about environment variables. A pin whose diagnostic is opaque converts into someone deleting the assertion, which is the round-3 reviewer's own argument and it applies here. THE FIX IS THREE LINES: print the findings list on failure (an `expect` variant that takes a diagnostic, or simply assert `_l07_env_findings(_L07_SRC) == []` in a form whose failure carries the list), and name `_L07_SHELL_PINNED` in the label so the constant to update is greppable from the message. I also checked the near-duplicate constant risk: `_L07_CD_LINE` at scripts/selftest.py:20475 is `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."` and `_L07_SHELL_PINNED` at :20737 carries `CDPATH= cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."`, two constants describing the same line at two revisions, and a future edit to that line needs both. That is correct today (the first is applied to the old loop text) but it is a trap of its own and deserves a comment saying so.

N4 THE COUNTS AND THE ON-DISK CLAIM ARE EXACT, AND THE RESTORE ASSERTION HOLDS AS FAR AS IT CAN BE CHECKED. Reproduced in detached worktrees at cfae9b2: unmutated `python3 scripts/selftest.py` 3200 passed / 0 failed exit 0; shell-half branch on disk 3199 passed / 1 failed exit 1; `sh -c` read on disk 3199 passed / 1 failed exit 1; dying assertion in both is the both-halves guard, verbatim the label at scripts/selftest.py:20805. The manifest's `where they previously survived at 3198 / 0' is the round-3 reviewer's figure at 405d3b3 and is attributed. BYTE-IDENTICAL RESTORE: I cannot audit the builder's own restores, which happened in a worktree that no longer exists, but I can and did check the two things that stand for it - scripts/check_lint.sh in the main working tree is byte-identical to cfae9b2 (sha256 4732323acec47152...), and the tree was clean before I started and is clean now except my own verdict. After each of my five on-disk mutations I restored and asserted the same digest, and all three worktrees matched. THE +2 IS EXACT AND THE ACCOUNT OF IT IS RIGHT: 25 expect() calls in the block at 405d3b3, 27 at cfae9b2, one replaced and two added, which is why three assertions changed while the count rises by two.

N5 THE TIMING RANGE IS ARITHMETICALLY CORRECT AND STILL EXCLUDES THE ROUND-3 REVIEWER'S LOWEST BEFORE-RUN, IN A SENTENCE THAT SAYS `ACROSS FOUR ROUNDS'. The manifest's AC3 evidence[2] reads `THE BEFORE FIGURES SPAN 13.96 TO 14.55 SECONDS AND THE AFTER FIGURES 0.79 TO 0.85 ACROSS FOUR ROUNDS' and then enumerates THREE measurers: this builder, the round-1 reviewer, the round-2 reviewer. The round-3 reviewer measured 13.89 / 14.13 / 14.06 at 7df08a1 and wrote it down explicitly, `my lowest before-run is 0.07s below the manifest's stated 13.96 floor ... which would move the ratio floor to 16.3x'. That figure is neither incorporated nor mentioned, while the sentence claims four rounds of coverage. My own before-runs are 13.99 / 14.07 / 13.96, so I do not widen it further, and the range errs WIDE rather than flattering in the direction that matters (the ratio floor is understated by 0.1x, not overstated). It is a provenance inaccuracy in one sentence, resolved either by writing 13.89 to 14.55 and 16.3x to 18.4x, or by saying `three measurers' instead of `across four rounds'. Everything else in that evidence block checks out: the conditions are stated, the cold run is disclosed rather than dropped, and the published means all sit inside the range.

N6 A CARRIED-FORWARD COUNT, THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SAME SLIP CLASS IN THIS MANIFEST LINEAGE. The producer field and assumptions[0] both say round 4 exists for `TWO OF TEN NOTES' of verdict-3. verdict-3 carries EIGHT notes, N1 through N8; TEN is verdict-2's count. The load-bearing half is true either way (the two notes closed are verdict-3's N1 and N2, and I confirmed both are the ones addressed), so this is a stale denominator rather than a wrong claim. It is worth one line only because it is the third of its kind: round 2's N3 caught `eight paths' for three commits, round 3's N5 caught `nine paths' for five commits, and this is `ten notes' for eight. THE PATH COUNT ITSELF IS NOW CORRECT, which I checked because round 3 flagged it: `git log --format='' --name-only cf20743~1..cfae9b2 | sort -u` is EXACTLY NINE distinct paths across exactly seven commits, so `Across all seven commits the item names nine paths' is right, and adding the eighth commit makes it ten. Numbers derived from a command are coming out right; numbers written from memory are still coming out one or two off.

N7 THE DECLARED LIMITS ARE ACCURATE, AND ONE IS DECLARED MORE PESSIMISTICALLY THAN IT BEHAVES. I attacked each declaration rather than reading it. BASH_ENV pointing at a file containing `echo "lint: pass"; exit 0`: `lint: pass' exit 0 over the eight-defect tree, so the declaration is accurate and it does run before line 1. PYTHONPATH pointing at a directory containing a hostile `subprocess.py`: `lint: pass' exit 0, accurate. PYTHONHOME pointing at a non-existent prefix: exit 1 with the interpreter unable to start and NO summary line, which FAILS CLOSED. So PYTHONHOME is named in a list of things that produce a false pass when as measured it produces a hard failure. That is the safe direction and I am not asking for it to be removed; it is worth knowing that the declared set is conservative rather than tight, and the honest form is `PYTHONPATH decides which subprocess the heredoc imports; PYTHONHOME breaks the interpreter outright, which fails closed'.

N8 WHAT ROUND 4 BROKE: NOTHING I CAN FIND, AND THE CHAIN IS CORRECT. The gate is GREEN at 2fd3d21 with 3200 passed / 0 failed on my own run, so no previously passing assertion regressed, and the two new assertions are the two the manifest names. `.warp/validate.py proof proof/WARP-0711/manifest.json` exits 0, the same for all three committed verdict files, and `.warp/validate.py all` exits 0. The manifest's `proof_digest` recomputes to `sha256:09bb64a3b435553d`, which is what it stores. THE SUPERSEDES CHAIN IS CORRECT ACROSS ALL FOUR MANIFESTS, read at the revision each landed: a1b16aa carries round 1 / commit cf20743 / supersedes_verdict null; 301dbd6 carries round 2 / commit a1b16aa / supersedes verdict-fail.json; cfae9b2 carries round 3 / commit 301dbd6 / supersedes verdict-2; 2fd3d21 carries round 4 / commit cfae9b2 / supersedes verdict-3. Each verdict file has exactly ONE commit in `git log --follow` and none was ever modified after it landed: verdict-fail.json at d4addf8, verdict-2 at 405d3b3, verdict-3 at 2fd3d21 committed unchanged as the record this round answers. The two events appended to .warp/events.jsonl are `gate.passed' at 405d3b3 and at cfae9b2, which is exactly the two gate runs claimed.

N10 HOUSEKEEPING, INCLUDING MY OWN, AND ONE SELF-INFLICTED FALSE RED WORTH RECORDING. MINE ARE GONE: the five detached worktrees I created (/tmp/w0711-head at 2fd3d21 for the gate run, /tmp/w0711-before at 7df08a1 for the before-timing, and /tmp/w0711-rev4, /tmp/w0711-m2, /tmp/w0711-m3 at cfae9b2 as mutation labs) are removed with `git worktree remove --force`, `git worktree prune` is clean, and `git worktree list` returns EXACTLY THREE ENTRIES: /path/to/repo at 2fd3d21 [main], /path/to/repo/WARP-0623 at f5d36ee, and /tmp/warp-w7-rev at 70a9ecb (detached), the last two being other sessions' and not mine to remove.
